stories.headline: US envoys meet Putin in Moscow as Russia orders three-day pause in Kyiv strikes
stories.body:
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday [c1, c13].

Kirill Dmitriev, who is Putin's investment envoy, received the two American envoys in the Russian capital [c20]. US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Witkoff and Kushner were bringing a proposal to end the war [c5]. Russian state media reported that the meeting between Putin and the envoys at the Kremlin lasted three hours [c6]. At the start of the meeting, Putin said it is convenient for Russia to work with Witkoff and Kushner [c19]. But Putin also told the envoys that the current situation is not so easy [c2].

During the meeting, Witkoff thanked Putin for agreeing with Ukraine to stop strikes on each other's capital cities for three days [c3]. Putin ordered a three-day halt to strikes on Kyiv because of the visit by the US envoys [c8]. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Putin gave the order to stop strikes starting from midnight Saturday [c14]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday [c7]. Witkoff and Kushner are scheduled to travel to Kyiv on Sunday for diplomatic engagements [c4]. CIA Director John Ratcliffe made a rare visit to Moscow a little over a week before Witkoff and Kushner arrived [c12].

Putin said in televised remarks that Russia has not agreed to a ceasefire in areas of Ukraine outside of Kyiv [c9]. Ground troops in Ukraine remain locked along a 775-mile frontline [c18]. Zelensky said Russia fired demonstrative strikes on airports in Kyiv and Boryspil overnight before his planned meeting with the envoys [c10]. On Friday, a Russian drone hit the headquarters of the Security Service of Ukraine [c17]. Russian strikes killed at least seven people across Ukraine on Saturday, including two in the Bucha district outside Kyiv [c15]. Zelensky said an overnight Russian strike on a civilian building in the Dnipro region killed four people and injured five others [c11]. Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the local military administration, said an overnight Russian strike at a factory in the Dnipropetrovsk region killed five people and wounded five others [c16].

vocab.meaning: A messenger or official representative sent by a government.
To stop oneself from doing something.

stories.headline: US military disables three Iranian oil tankers following attacks on warships
stories.body:
US Central Command said its forces permanently disabled two Iran-linked oil tankers and completely destroyed a third in the Gulf of Oman [c21]. US Central Command said the strikes retaliated after Tehran targeted a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer [c22]. US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth posted on social media that if Iran shoots at US ships, the US will destroy and sink their oil tankers [c25]. US Central Command commander Admiral Brad Cooper said the US military would destroy Iran's oil fleet if necessary to defend American forces [c30].

US Central Command identified the disabled tankers as M/T Downy, struck off Kharg Island, and M/T Stark 1, struck near Jask [c32]. Kharg Island hosts Iran's main oil export terminal, handling about 90% of the country's crude oil exports via pipes from the mainland [c23]. US Central Command identified the destroyed third tanker as M/T Kylo, which is also known as Noxen [c33].

The US resumed attacks after striking two rocket launchers to stop Iran from laying naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz [c26]. Iranian state media reported that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps retaliated against six ships [c24]. These included three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and three US-affiliated vessels [c24].

US Vice President JD Vance said he was extremely sceptical about Iranian claims that US strikes killed four people at a wedding in Sirik [c28]. A preliminary US military inquiry found a February 28 strike on a school compound in Minab killed at least 156 people [c31]. The inquiry found outdated coordinates had identified the school as part of a naval base [c31]. The average price for a gallon of diesel in the US reached $5.85, up from $3.71 a year prior [c27].

vocab.meaning: Paid back an attack with a similar action.
Coming before the main or final part.

stories.headline: Rescuers pull survivors from wreckage days after flood disaster in Nepal and China
stories.body:
Rescue teams pulled survivors from flood wreckage in Nepal and China days after a massive disaster [c34, c35, c40]. Rescuers pulled Chandika Kumari Shrestha, who is 64 years old, semi-conscious from a buried house in Betrawati 10 days after floods hit Nepal [c34]. Local officials in Betrawati said only five out of about 300 houses remained standing after the flood [c37]. A joint team of Nepal army personnel and South Korean experts rescued Chinese worker Luhaitao from a tunnel [c35, c36]. Luhaitao was rescued 225 metres inside a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project and flown to a military hospital [c35, c36]. The Upper Trishuli-1 project is valued at about $647m [c44].

A collapse of ice, rock, and mud swept through a Himalayan valley in Nepal [c38]. Nepal's national disaster authority reported that the flood killed at least 1,331 people [c39]. Nepal's disaster management agency reported that at least 1,375 people died [c45]. The disaster left about 5,000 people missing, including 589 foreign nationals [c39, c45]. Officials in Tibet recorded 31 deaths and 531 people missing across the border [c40].

About 900 workers remain unaccounted for at hydropower construction sites in Nepal, with roughly 500 believed trapped inside tunnels [c41]. The floods severely damaged 12 hydropower plants in the Trishuli River basin and knocked out over 10% of Nepal's power capacity [c43]. Nearly 100% of Nepal's electricity comes from hydropower [c42].

vocab.meaning: A sudden event that causes great destruction or loss.
The total amount that something can produce or contain.

stories.headline: UN adopts resolution approving world map that shows true size of countries
stories.body:
The United Nations voted on Friday to support moving away from the 16th-century Mercator map toward a map showing true country sizes [c46]. The UN General Assembly adopted the Correct the Map resolution to fix discrepancies in the Mercator map projection [c47]. Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator created the Mercator map in 1569 to aid European sailors in ocean navigation [c49]. The African continent is about 14 times larger than Greenland, despite looking similar in size on the Mercator map [c48].

Togo introduced the resolution at the UN on behalf of 54 African member states, supported by the African Union [c56]. Togo's Foreign Minister Robert Dussey said a fair map does not change geography, but changes how the world is seen [c54]. A team of cartographers created the Equal Earth projection in 2018, and African Union members adopted it in February [c50].

The UN resolution passed with 164 countries voting in favour, one voting against, and six abstaining [c51]. India voted in favour of the resolution, while the United States was the only country to vote against it [c52]. US representative Yaryna Ferencevych said resolutions like Correct the Map cause the UN to lose credibility [c57]. The US delegation claimed the resolution was part of a larger radical political project [c55]. Ukraine abstained over concerns about how some Equal Earth maps depict Ukrainian territories occupied by Russia [c53].

vocab.meaning: A way of showing the curved surface of the Earth on a flat map.
Chose not to vote for or against something.

stories.headline: PM Modi addresses SRCC centenary, defends GDP growth and warns Pakistan
stories.body:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the centenary celebrations at Shri Ram College of Commerce in Delhi on Saturday evening [c58]. Modi previously spoke at the college in February 2013 while serving as Chief Minister of Gujarat [c59]. Modi recalled his 2013 glass analogy, saying he sees the glass as full, with half water and half air [c60]. Modi is serving his third consecutive term as Prime Minister and completes 25 years as head of government next month [c65].

Modi cited India's first-quarter GDP growth rate of 7.8 per cent as evidence of economic strength [c61]. Modi described critics of the GDP growth numbers as grumpy uncles who focus only on negativity [c62]. Modi said those who placed India among the fragile five economies cannot digest India's 7.8 per cent growth [c66].

Former senior Finance Ministry official Subhash Chandra Garg claimed the 7.8 per cent growth rate was overstated due to base revisions [c67]. Garg said nominal GDP growth would be 2.6 per cent if the previous year's base was not revised down [c68]. Former RBI Governor Raghuram Rajan asked why strong growth has not led to higher private investment and job creation [c69]. India's Ministry of Statistics held a press briefing to defend the revised GDP methodology implemented in February [c70].

Congress leader Kanhaiya Kumar called Modi's address a public relations campaign before student elections [c73]. Kumar said Modi focused on 2013 and 2047 while failing to address student or public issues [c64]. Congress MP Pawan Khera criticized Modi's speech on social media, writing that even onions would burst into tears [c63].

Modi criticized the Congress party's student outreach campaign, called Chhatron Ki Goonj, describing it as an echo of lies [c74]. The campaign focuses on student issues including exam paper leaks, rising education costs, and unemployment [c75]. Modi said if Pakistan indulges in misadventure, Indian armed forces enter their territory and strike [c71]. Modi said his Independence Day reference to urban Naxals exposed political opponents like a homeopathic dose [c72].

vocab.meaning: A hundredth anniversary or its celebration.
A system of methods used in a particular area of study or activity.

stories.headline: Indian government advances Census enumeration in four poll-bound states
stories.body:
The Indian government advanced the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 in four states [c76]. The enumeration in Uttar Pradesh, Goa, Punjab, and non-snow-bound Uttarakhand will run from December 1, 2026, to January 4, 2027 [c76]. The reference date for the advanced Census enumeration in these four states is set for January 5, 2027 [c77]. A revisional round for Census enumeration in these four states will take place from January 5 to January 9, 2027 [c82]. A 15-day self-enumeration window for Census 2027 will open in the four states from November 16 to November 30, 2026 [c78].

Assembly elections are scheduled to take place in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Goa, and Manipur in February-March 2027 [c79]. Government officials said dates were advanced to prevent staffing conflicts between census duties and elections [c83].

The Census phase in Manipur was deferred following local demands to conduct the National Register of Citizens exercise first [c80]. The Ministry of Home Affairs deferred the Manipur census on August 31 amid ongoing state violence [c84].

Census 2027 will be India's first digital census and will collect caste data for the first time since 1931 [c81]. The national population census was originally scheduled for 2021 but was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic [c85].

vocab.meaning: The act of counting or listing things one by one.
Put off to a later time; postponed.
